```{python}
#| label: fig-supply-trend
#| echo: false
#| fig-cap: "Nominal core supply voltage versus CMOS technology node. Below roughly 90 nm, the supply voltage no longer scales with the feature size but flattens out around 1 V, limited by the subthreshold leakage (data after Stillmaker and Baas, 2017)."

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

# Stillmaker, A., & Baas, B. (2017). Scaling equations for the accurate
# prediction of CMOS device performance from 180 nm to 7 nm.
# Integration, 58, 74-81.
data = [
    (1.0, 5), (0.8, 5), (0.5, 5), (0.35, 3.3), (0.25, 2.5), (0.18, 1.8),
    (0.13, 1.2), (0.090, 1.1), (0.065, 1.1), (0.045, 1.1), (0.032, 0.97),
    (0.020, 0.9), (0.016, 0.86), (0.010, 0.83), (0.007, 0.8),
]

feat = [d[0] for d in data]
vdd = [d[1] for d in data]

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(6, 4))
ax.semilogx(feat, vdd, 'o-', color='tab:blue', lw=2, ms=5)
ax.invert_xaxis()
ax.set_xlabel('Feature size (µm)')
ax.set_ylabel('Supply voltage $V_\\mathrm{DD}$ (V)')
ax.set_ylim(0, 6)
ax.grid(True, which='both', alpha=0.3)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```
